s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive weakness, fatigue, and confusion with a mediastinal mass and pulmonary emboli
salient_findings: Increasing weakness, fatigue, and confusion over a few weeks
Lobar and segmental pulmonary emboli in right middle and lower lobes
key_facts: 67-year-old man with a history of mood disorder, Parkinson's disease, hyperlipidemia, and mild cognitive impairment
Presented after an unwitnessed fall at home
Reported decreased appetite and mild dyspnea, especially on exertion
No significant weight loss, dysphagia, or odynophagia
No history of smoking
Elevated serum creatinine: 3.7 mg/dL (327 μmol/L)
Hemoglobin: 10.5 g/dL (105 g/L)
α-fetoprotein and β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels: normal
CT head and C-spine: unremarkable
CT chest: lobulated anterior mediastinal mass
Contrast CT chest: showed lobar and segmental pulmonary emboli
MRI brain with and without contrast: no intracranial mass lesion
Immunohistochemistry: Positive for P40 immunostain
Negative for thyroid transcription factor-1 and napsin A immunostains

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of anterior mediastinal mass

shortlist.label: Thymic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor that can present with systemic symptoms and mediastinal mass

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma

shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the patient's age and presence of a mediastinal mass

raw.rationale: The patient has a lobulated anterior mediastinal mass with positive P40 immunostain and negative thyroid transcription factor-1 and napsin A immunostains, which is consistent with squamous cell carcinoma, especially given the provided figure title 'Squamous cell carcinoma from a mediastinal mass'

rejected.label: Thymoma
rejected.why: Thymomas are typically associated with positive staining for thyroid transcription factor-1, which is negative in this case

rejected.label: Thymic carcinoma
rejected.why: While thymic carcinoma can present similarly, the specific immunohistochemistry profile and the provided figure title support squamous cell carcinoma more directly

rejected.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: The description and immunohistochemistry results do not align with typical findings for non-Hodgkin lymphoma

rejected.label: Mediastinal metastasis
rejected.why: The presence of a primary mediastinal mass with specific immunohistochemical markers suggests a primary tumor rather than a metastasis
